intro: Biochemists and biophysicists solve complex scientific problems and teach others, skills shared with physics and engineering research. The closest of the 25 careers below is Physicists, with an 86% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $172,250, which is 35% more than the $127,410 biochemists and biophysicists earn.
why_it_works: Research means designing experiments, interpreting messy data and explaining results to colleagues and funders. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 4.12 out of 5 for this job and judgment at 4. Physics, nanosystems and biomedical engineering use the same depth. All 25 matches need no more education than you already have. The gaps are technology design and managing budgets.
tips: Medical Dosimetrists earn $147,470, which is 16% more, and apply physics to patient care.
Computer Hardware Engineers earn $161,740, or 27% more, if you enjoy instruments and electronics.
Grant management experience helps with research leadership; managing money is a common gap.

faq.q: What jobs can former biochemists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Physicists (86%), nanosystems engineers (85%) and Bioengineers and Biomedical Engineers (80%), based on O*NET 31.0. Biomedical engineers earn $109,370, which is 14% less than the $127,410 median for biochemists and biophysicists, but often work closer to products and patients.

faq.q: Which careers for biochemists pay more?
faq.a: 7 of the 25 matches pay more. Physicists earn $172,250 (35% more), Computer Hardware Engineers $161,740 (27% more) and Medical Dosimetrists $147,470 (16% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Most of these employers value a strong research background and lab experience.

faq.q: Do biochemists need another degree to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than biochemists and biophysicists already have, including all of the top 10. A doctoral degree is common, held by 49% of workers in the closest match, so your research training covers most requirements.

The skills that most often need work are technology design, service orientation, troubleshooting and managing financial resources. Instructing already rates 3.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so engineering design and budget skills are the main steps outside the lab.
